recipient: Robert Bowman, 123 West Main, Shelbyville, Il. 62565
notes: Front: a twilight photo of Fort Worth's downtown skyline reflected in a pond, titled simply “FORT WORTH” in bold magenta script — the kind of minimalist, photo-forward postcard design common in the 1980s. Back: “Fort Worth, Texas,” published by The Texas Postcard Company, Plano, TX (card F-116); printed by McGrew Color Graphics, Kansas City, Mo. (a postcard printer active from at least the 1970s onward); photo by Richard Stockton. No postmark or stamp is present — this card appears to have never gone through the mail, likely tucked into an envelope or handed over directly. Pencilled dealer/collector marks “1595” and “100” appear at the top — the same “1595” marking that has now turned up on more than one card in this collection, suggesting several of these postcards passed through the same dealer lot at some point. Message: “Hi! We are having a good time. Saw [?] graduate & also his[?] signed diploma. See you sometime. Student, Fred, Linda & Christy” — a few words here resist full confidence, but the gist is a graduation trip update. Addressed to Robert Bowman in Shelbyville, Illinois — the ZIP code (62565) confirms the card postdates 1963, and the skyline view is consistent with 1980s-era Fort Worth.
feed_description: An undated Fort Worth skyline postcard, never mailed — Fred, Linda & Christy write to Robert Bowman in Shelbyville, Illinois about a graduation trip.

location: Hector Falls, New York (near Watkins Glen)
address: Hector Falls, east shore of Seneca Lake, north of Watkins Glen, NY
recipient: Mrs. Lena Stafford, 71 Montreal St., Sanford, Maine 04073
notes: Front: a color photo of Hector Falls, a multi-tiered cascade over layered shale, framed by trees with a wooden viewing rail at the base. Back printed text: “Hector Falls — Is a sparkling gem, as it cascades over the rocky slope above the east shore of Seneca Lake, a few miles north of Watkins Glen, N.Y.” Published by Howard Champion, Watkins Glen, N.Y.; “Lustrachrome” process card made by Tichnor Bros., Inc., Boston. 6-cent Flag over White House stamp (first issued January 1968), postmark mostly illegible beyond a partial “...R. N.Y.” Combined with the ZIP code on the address (04073, Sanford, Maine, confirming a post-1963 date) and the 6¢ Flag stamp's common-use window, this card likely dates to around 1968–1971. Message: “Dear Staffy – Polly and I are on a trip to see the Burpees in New York. We went to this spot yesterday and hope to go to Niagara Falls before we come home. However the weather is not too good. Hope to be home by Wednesday. Time will tell. Much love, ‘Ma’ Hadden[s]” — a warm travel update from one older woman to another, touring the Finger Lakes region with a stop planned for Niagara Falls before heading home.
feed_description: A postcard from Hector Falls near Watkins Glen, NY — ‘Ma’ Hadden writes to a friend in Sanford, Maine about a Finger Lakes trip with a Niagara Falls stop still to come.

recipient: Herrn Albert Hueske, 509 Ave of Oaks, Houston, Tex. 77009, U.S.A.
notes: This card came in filed as “Unknown” — the front carries no printed caption — but the return address on the back gives it away: this is Trappenkamp itself. The aerial front photo shows a purpose-built settlement of identical red-roofed apartment blocks laid out along straight streets, ringed by heathland and forest with dunes and open water visible in the distance. Trappenkamp has a striking origin story: the town didn't exist before the 1930s. The site began as “Gönnebeker Heide,” a Prussian cavalry and infantry parade ground; in July 1934 the German Navy chose the site (by then state forest) to build a mine-storage depot relieving pressure on the naval arsenal at Kiel. British troops occupied it on 18 May 1945, and afterward it was repurposed as a refugee camp for Germans expelled from the eastern territories and the Sudetenland. It became its own independent municipality in April 1956, having previously been administered as part of neighboring Bornhöved. The front photo captures exactly this transformation — a former military depot reborn as row after row of refugee housing. The return address, written by the sender at the top of the card per German convention, reads “2351 Trappenkamp / Arndtstr. 31” — “2351” is an old West German four-digit postal code, consistent with a mid-20th-century date. A printed clearance code at the bottom, “Frei. Reg. Präs. Düss. 17-C 208,” is the kind of official image-rights approval stamp West German postcard publishers commonly carried at the time. Message (German): “Unser lieber Vetter Albert! Gottes Segen für Dein neues Lebensjahr, viel Glück, Freude u. Gesundheit für Dich u. Hildegard. Wo das X auf der Karte, in der Richtung wohnen wir. Viel schöne Stunden wünschen Euch in Liebe Eure Werner u. Hemchen.” Translation: “Our dear cousin Albert! God's blessing for your new year of life [i.e. happy birthday], much luck, joy and health for you and Hildegard. Where the X is on the card, that's the direction we live in. Wishing you many lovely hours, with love, your Werner and Hemchen.” Addressed to Albert Hueske at 509 Ave of Oaks, Houston, Texas — the very same street address as the Brauer family's Laredo postcard already in the archive (card #184) — very likely the same household or a close relative, both maintaining ties with German family back home. Worth a look for the Family Networks tag.
feed_description: A birthday greeting from Trappenkamp, Germany — a town built from a WWII naval depot turned refugee settlement — to cousin Albert Hueske at the same Houston address as another card already in the archive.
